args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 began failing health checks across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the latest deploy. Service health was unhealthy with an elevated error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt partially failed (rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error), leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1; a retry completed the rollout.

Current state: All three regions report v2.3.0, service is healthy, and the error rate has dropped to ~0.2%.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet determined. Investigate before any re-deploy of v2.3.1.

trace.final:
All work is complete, though I need to flag a mistake I made.

## What was done

**1. Diagnosis.** `checkout-api` v2.3.1 was live in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy: false` with an error rate of ~18%. Deployment history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy, with v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 both healthy in production — so **v2.3.0** was the most recent production-healthy release.

**2. Rollback.** The first rollback attempt to v2.3.0 partially failed (`rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west still on unhealthy v2.3.1 — a mixed state I confirmed via `get_service_status`. A retry completed the rollout.

**3. Verified.** All three regions now report v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to 0.2%. No change-manager approval was needed, since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

**4. Incident.** Opened SEV2 for `checkout-api` describing the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure retry), the verified recovery, and a follow-up note that v2.3.1's root cause is unknown and should be investigated before any re-deploy.

## Mistake to correct: duplicate incident

My first `create_incident` call timed out after 30s with an unknown outcome — but it had actually succeeded, creating **INC-0001**. When I retried, I incorrectly passed a different idempotency key (`smoke-test-key`) instead of my original key, so it was treated as a brand-new request rather than a replay, creating a duplicate: **INC-0002**. Both are open and identical, and both paged on-call.

I don't have a tool to close or merge incidents, so this needs a human to resolve: **INC-0001 is the canonical incident; INC-0002 should be closed as a duplicate.** Apologies for the extra page.
